note: TLS 1.3 loopback listener, POST-only MCP endpoint, header and body bounds, Host and Origin checks. No UDS listener, no Remote Access listener, no per-source connection limits.

Both protocol eras through the MCP Go SDK in stateless mode, method allowlist, cache hints, Appendix B codes with reasonCode, correlationId and decisionId. No progress relay, no data.message text (FR-1.51), no hold-mode keep-alives.

OAuth 2.1 authorization server (metadata, PKCE S256, resource, iss), pre-registered clients, Argon2id. Sign-in uses the Administrator password, not a Session Approver; metadata advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported without fetching documents; no DCR, mTLS or lockout.
Session store with lifetimes, per-principal limits, scope-to-template mapping, session API and refresh. Refresh tokens are not rotated; sessions do not survive restart; no taint tracking.
Schema-validated policy file compiled at startup. No signed Policy Store, publication, simulation, rollback or revision history.

Default-deny decisions over the compiled snapshot, approval obligation flag, sliding-window rate limits, decision IDs. No argument predicates, deny rules, explanations, secret-use or anomaly obligations.
An approval-obligated call is refused with -31002; no approval records, hold mode, CLI, console or notification.
Session-scoped catalog per policy revision, unknown-tool rejection, approval hint (FR-1.50). No metadata scan at presentation.
schema-validate request filter only. No path, URL, secret, injection or Unicode filters; no versioned rule sets.
stdio dispatch with concurrency and queue bounds, upstream timeout, result size bound and backend error mapping. Instances are shared across sessions; no cancellation propagation or progress relay.
Result size bound and provenance metadata marking results untrusted. No content filters, output-schema validation or delimiting.

One-use launch capability, pre-launch and pre-release rechecks, in-memory emergency stop. The authorized event is appended after the capability is issued and is not flushed per call, so SR-6.2-1 and SR-6.3-1 are not yet met.
No package verification or smcpctl package commands; tools are read from live backends at startup.
In-memory registry from the live tool list: public-name derivation, collision refusal, tool definition validity checks. No manifests, enablement states, drift suspension or artifact cache.
Launches configured commands as child processes with an environment allowlist and bounded stderr capture. Launch commands are not restricted to packaged artifacts (the bootstrap example uses npx).
No sandbox; backends run unconfined.

Mandatory event floor to signed, hash-chained JSON Lines segments and the smcpctl journal verify checker. Events are flushed only when a segment closes; no graph mirror feed, export or key transitions.

Local CA and listener certificate, Ed25519 evidence key, Argon2id hashing. CA has five-year validity and no name constraints; keys are 0600 files without TPM, Keychain or passphrase; no trust anchors or rotation.
GET /healthz reports fail-closed for emergency stop or a missing snapshot. No periodic checks, profiles, diagnostic log or metrics.

smcpctl bootstrap, config validate, journal verify, health and hash-password; TOML configuration validated against a JSON Schema. No control API, console, install, upgrade, approvals or backup commands.
No smcp-session, smcp-stdio, smcp-connect, doctor or lockdown profiles.
